title: Fenlara Execution Offer
description: This schema describes an EXECUTION OFFER — the only object Fenlara reasons about. It does not describe the Fenlara engine, a discovery protocol, or an agent identity system. Fenlara does not standardize what an agent is, how it is discovered, or how it is verified; it only defines the minimal, flat contract an offer must satisfy to be selectable. Upstream systems (DAWN-style discovery, A2A Agent Cards, ANP descriptions, private registries...) are expected to normalize their own richer records down to this shape before calling select().

offer_id.description: REQUIRED, DECISION KEY. Unique identifier of this specific execution offer. Every key in a SelectionResult (scores, rejections, chosen.offer_id) is an offer_id. Two offers from the same agent MUST have different offer_id values.

agent_id.description: REQUIRED, AUDIT METADATA — not a decision input. Fenlara never branches a constraint or a score on agent_id; it is carried through unread by the decision logic and only reattached in the final result, so the caller can trace a chosen offer back to the agent that issued it, and so several offers from the same agent can be told apart without being treated specially.

protocol.description: DECISION INPUT (conditional) — read only if the request supplies a 'required_protocol' constraint, compared for exact equality. Fenlara has no built-in list of valid protocols — 'a2a', 'anp', 'mcp', or any future value are all opaque strings to it. An offer has exactly one protocol; an agent with several communication options publishes several offers.

jurisdiction.description: DECISION INPUT (conditional) — read only if the request supplies a 'jurisdiction' constraint, compared for exact equality. Fenlara does not validate this against any real-world list of jurisdictions.

price.description: DECISION INPUT (conditional) — read by the 'max_price' constraint (if present) and by the 'price' preference criterion (lower is better, normalized against the surviving pool). No currency is implied or enforced by Fenlara — that agreement must exist upstream.

latency_ms.description: DECISION INPUT (conditional) — read by the 'max_latency_ms' constraint (if present) and by the 'latency' preference criterion (lower is better). Fenlara treats this as a self-reported number, not a measured guarantee.

trust.description: DECISION INPUT (conditional) — read only by the 'trust' preference criterion (higher is better). Fenlara does not compute this value and cannot verify it — it is trusted as published. Computing and attesting trust is a discovery/registry-layer concern (see e.g. AINS's evidence model), not a Fenlara concern.

availability.description: DECISION INPUT (conditional) — read only by the 'availability' preference criterion (higher is better). Purely a snapshot value at selection time — Fenlara makes no freshness or liveness guarantee about it; re-verification before connecting is the Resolution layer's job.

capabilities.description: PASSTHROUGH. Fenlara does not match, filter, or score on capabilities — it assumes the offer already matches the requester's intent by the time it reaches selection (that matching happens upstream, in Discovery). Carried through only so the caller doesn't need a second lookup.

endpoint.description: PASSTHROUGH. Fenlara never dereferences, calls, or validates this URL. It is opaque data handed to the Resolution/Connection layers once an offer is chosen.

$comment: additionalProperties is deliberately true: an offer may carry any amount of extra metadata Fenlara doesn't know about. Unknown FIELDS on an offer are always ignored. This is distinct from an unknown CONSTRAINT KEY in a selection request, which Fenlara rejects fail-closed — an unrecognized field you didn't ask about is harmless; an unrecognized filter you did ask for and got silently ignored is not.
